# `proposal/v1` — proposals/<id>.md — proposal file

<!-- AUTOGENERATED from `Glorbo.FileSpec.ProposalMd` by
     `mix glorbo.docs.file_formats`. Do not edit by hand;
     regen after changing the spec module. -->

Agent-created structural proposals (GEP-28). Used for hiring,
firing, budget changes, new projects, and custom requests that
require Director approval. Frontmatter-driven approval flow;
auto-approval within headcount budget for hire/fire subtypes.

## Frontmatter schema

**Required:** `kind`, `id`, `subtype`, `status`, `proposed_by`, `requires_approval`, `proposed_at`

**Optional:** `approved_by`, `approved_at`, `denial_reason`, `superseded_by`

### Enums

| Key | Allowed values |
|-----|----------------|
| `requires_approval` | `director` |
| `status` | `pending-approval`, `approved`, `denied`, `superseded` |
| `subtype` | `hire`, `fire`, `budget`, `project`, `custom` |


## Canonical key order

When the formatter rewrites this file, keys appear in this order:

`kind`, `id`, `subtype`, `status`, `proposed_by`, `requires_approval`, `proposed_at`, `approved_by`, `approved_at`, `denial_reason`, `superseded_by`

Unknown keys fall after the known block, sorted alphabetically.

## Examples

```markdown
---
kind: proposal/v1
id: hire-writer-2026-04-21
subtype: hire
status: pending-approval
proposed_by: ceo
requires_approval: director
proposed_at: 2026-04-21T10:00:00Z
---

## Rationale

We need a Writer to handle the editorial calendar.

## Execution hint

```bash
glorbo new agent techblog/writer --role writer --provider opencode
```
